newsitem.title: USA: Olin Corp. net drops as chemical prices decline.
newsitem.headline: Olin Corp. net drops as chemical prices decline.

text.p: Chemicals manufacturer Olin Corp. said Thursday its profits fell 25 percent for the second quarter, hurt by lower prices for its chlor alkali chemical products.
The Norwalk, Conn.-based company said second-quarter net income declined to $38.6 million, or 75 cents a share, from $51.7 million, or $1.01 a share, a year ago.
Sales slipped to $632.4 million on the quarter from $701.7 million in the same year-ago period.

The results primarily reflect lower pricing in the chlor alkali industry, as well as a slower-than-anticipated recovery in certain microelectronic material markets, said company Chairman Donald Griffin.
"We expect that tight supply-demand will increase pricing for our chlor alkali products and that demand will accelerate for our microelectronic materials as the year progresses," he said.

Operating income from its chemicals unit fell to $46 million for the quarter, compared with $65.7 million a year ago. Metals and ammunition operating income was $12.6 million, compared with $14 million a year ago.
The company's stock fell 37.5 cents to $39.81 in consolidated midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
